title: An immutable schedule

blocks.text: The page's strongest protection is an **immutable object**: once made, its state never changes, so there is nothing to guard. The page also warns that **subclassing can break encapsulation**: a subclass could add mutable state or override behaviour, so an immutable class is declared `final`.
Write `Schedule`, an immutable list of time slots with a name:

items: `String getName()` and `List<String> getSlots()`: the slots can be read but not changed through the returned list;
`Schedule withSlot(String slot)` returns a **new** schedule with `slot` added at the end. The schedule it was called on stays as it was.

blocks.text: Changing the list passed to the constructor afterwards does not change the schedule. The class cannot be extended, and every field it declares is `private` and `final`.

cases.says: withSlot returns a schedule with the same name and the new slot added at the end.
After withSlot, and after a caller tries to change the returned slots, the original schedule still has its old slots.
Schedule cannot be subclassed, and every field it declares is private and final.
Changing the list passed to the constructor afterwards does not change the schedule.

concepts: An immutable object, whose state never changes after construction, is the strongest data protection.
Subclassing can break encapsulation, so a class that must stay protected is made final.
